tag.en: Python · LangGraph · agent with a critic

summary.pt: Faça uma pergunta de mercado. O agente planeja as seções, busca fontes (com retry), escreve citando cada fonte, passa por um crítico que confere fontes e números, refaz o que falhar e entrega um relatório. Se a fonte cair ou não houver evidência, ele diz isso em vez de inventar.
summary.en: Ask a market question. The agent plans the sections, retrieves sources (with retries), writes citing every source, passes through a critic that checks sources and numbers, redoes what fails and returns a report. If a source is down or evidence is missing, it says so instead of making things up.

note.pt: Fontes fictícias sobre assinaturas de café especial. Temas que ele cobre: mercado, preço, concorrência, churn, canais, logística. Tente a segunda predefinição (fontes fora do ar) e a quarta (tema sem fonte). O redator desta demo é determinístico, não um modelo de linguagem.
note.en: Fictional sources about specialty coffee subscriptions. Topics covered: market, pricing, competition, churn, channels, logistics. Try the second preset (sources down) and the fourth (topic with no source). This demo's writer is deterministic, not a language model.

message.en: ETIMEDOUT: the search service did not answer (simulated)

problem.pt: Analistas gastam horas juntando dados de várias fontes para um briefing de mercado e, na pressa, citam número sem fonte ou esquecem de avisar que uma fonte estava fora.
problem.en: Analysts spend hours stitching data from several sources into a market brief and, in a hurry, quote numbers without a source or forget to say a source was unreachable.

solution.pt: Um grafo LangGraph com estado: planejador, recuperação com retry, redator, crítico e laço de revisão. O crítico recusa seção com menos de 2 fontes ou com número que não está na fonte citada; a revisão amplia a busca uma vez. Fonte inacessível vira nota no relatório; tema sem evidência vira "não há evidência suficiente".
solution.en: A stateful LangGraph graph: planner, retrieval with retries, writer, critic and a revision loop. The critic rejects a section with fewer than 2 sources or with a number that is not in the cited source; the revision widens the search once. An unreachable source becomes a note in the report; a topic with no evidence becomes "not enough evidence".

gain.pt: Estimativa, não medição: se um briefing manual leva ~90 min e a primeira versão automática leva ~2 min mais ~15 min de revisão humana, são cerca de 70 min por briefing. O ganho real depende de as fontes certas estarem no corpus; com modelo de linguagem de verdade, a qualidade do texto muda e o crítico continua sendo a barreira.
gain.en: An estimate, not a measurement: if a manual brief takes ~90 min and the first automatic draft takes ~2 min plus ~15 min of human review, that is about 70 min per brief. Real gain depends on the right sources being in the corpus; with a real language model the prose changes and the critic remains the guardrail.

pt: python agent.py "market size, pricing and churn for coffee subscriptions" --out out
en: python agent.py "market size, pricing and churn for coffee subscriptions" --out out

honesty.pt: O grafo, a busca, o crítico e o relatório rodam aqui com a mesma lógica do código Python (conferido contra as saídas gravadas). O redator é um gerador determinístico que monta frases a partir das fontes; um modelo local via Ollama entra no mesmo ponto (classe OllamaLLM), mas não foi testado nesta máquina. Fontes e números são fictícios. Tempos e a falha simulada são ilustrativos.
honesty.en: The graph, search, critic and report run here with the same logic as the Python code (checked against recorded outputs). The writer is a deterministic generator that assembles sentences from the sources; a local model through Ollama plugs in at the same point (OllamaLLM class) but was not tested on this machine. Sources and numbers are fictional. Timings and the simulated failure are illustrative.

footer.pt: Dados fictícios. Nada é enviado: tudo roda no seu navegador.
footer.en: Fictional data. Nothing is sent: everything runs in your browser.

input.question: What is the market size, pricing and competition for coffee subscriptions, and what about churn?

expect.report:
# Research brief

**Question:** What is the market size, pricing and competition for coffee subscriptions, and what about churn?

_Model: mock-deterministic. Every claim carries a source id; the list is at the end._

## Market size and growth

Specialty coffee subscriptions reached US$ 2.4 billion in 2025, up 18% from 2024. [d01] A panel of 3,200 buyers found 61% subscribe for convenience and 27% for discovery of new roasters. [d02]

## Pricing

The median 250 g bag costs US$ 14.50 on subscription and US$ 16.90 on single purchase. [d03] Shipping a 250 g bag costs US$ 4.80 on average, 33% of the subscription price. [d07]

## Competition

Five regional roasters hold 38% of subscription revenue. [d04] Bean Harbor lowered its entry plan to US$ 12.90 in September 2025 and added a skip-a-month option. [d08]

## Retention and churn

Monthly churn is 9% in the first three months and 4% afterwards. [d05] Bean Harbor lowered its entry plan to US$ 12.90 in September 2025 and added a skip-a-month option. [d08]

## Sources

- [d01] Specialty Coffee Subscription Market 2025 (fictional) (https://example.invalid/market-2025)
- [d02] Consumer Panel: Who Subscribes (fictional) (https://example.invalid/panel)
- [d03] Pricing Benchmark: Whole Bean Bags (fictional) (https://example.invalid/pricing)
- [d04] Competitor Scan: Five Regional Players (fictional) (https://example.invalid/competitors)
- [d05] Retention Study: First 90 Days (fictional) (https://example.invalid/retention)
- [d07] Logistics Cost Note (fictional) (https://example.invalid/logistics)
- [d08] Competitor Pricing Move (fictional) (https://example.invalid/bean-harbor)
